QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_15

question.text: Saraswati Cat II AIF returns the following to LPs over its life: Return of capital INR 200 crore; Preferred return at 8% hurdle INR 40 crore; Total profits above capital INR 100 crore (i.e., total distributions INR 300 crore against INR 200 crore called capital). The waterfall has an 8% hurdle, 100% GP catch-up, and 80/20 carry split thereafter. How much carry does the GP receive in total?

explanation.text: The Logic: Profit above capital = 100 cr. With 100% GP catch-up + 80/20 carry, the GP receives 20% of TOTAL profits above capital. Carry = 20% x 100 = INR 20 crore. Step-by-step: (1) return 200 cr capital, (2) LP gets 8% pref = 40 cr, (3) GP catch-up = 40 x 20/80 = 10 cr (until GP has 20% of cumulative pref+catch-up = 10), (4) remaining 100 - 40 - 10 = 50 cr split 80/20 = LP 40 cr + GP 10 cr. GP total = 10 + 10 = 20 cr. The Trap: INR 10 crore counts only the catch-up. INR 30 crore double-counts. INR 40 crore would be 20% of total distributions (wrong — carry is 20% of profit, not of total). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical waterfall math. XIX-A distributor version may test only the hurdle concept. XXI-B PMS exam tests high-water-mark performance fees (different mechanic). Manager's Pro-Tip: Always keep your waterfall schedule in Excel AND in a PDF appendix to the PPM with numerical examples. LPs who see the math pre-commit rarely dispute the GP catch-up math post-exit — it is the disputed catch-up that kills Fund II fundraises.
